title: Settlement Agreements Alongside Payment Arrangements and Hardship Holds
content:
# Settlement Agreements — Interplay with Payment Arrangements and Hardship Holds

A settlement under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements and a payment plan under its Payment Arrangements never run together on one account, and a hold under its Hardship and Protective Holds changes which settlements may be offered.

## Payment plans

- An offer may be extended on an account that has a plan in any status.
- When the consumer accepts, any plan on that account in pending authorization, active, suspended or broken status is cancelled the same day with the closing reason superseded by settlement.
- Installments already paid stay applied to the account and reduce the balance, not the settlement amount.
- The plan is cancelled and any hardship hold the acceptance ends is ended before the acceptance itself, so the account is in active status when the acceptance moves it to arranged.

## Hardship holds and offers

- An offer on an account in hardship hold status is extended only when the tier of the hold in force allows settlement offers during the hold.
- **Qualifying hold for a Hardship Settlement.** A Hardship Settlement is offered only when the account's most recent hardship hold is in status active, or has status ended with an ended date no more than that hold tier's post-hold hardship window in calendar days before the offer date, and in every case that hold tier makes the account eligible for a Hardship Settlement after the hold.

> The qualifying-hold clause above is **no longer in force** as a basis for Two-Payment Settlement and Three-Payment Settlement offers priced under the current pricing rules for those programmes; for those offers it is superseded by the current basis of each rule.

- A hardship hold denied, withdrawn or ended outside the window never qualifies, and a consumer's statement of hardship without a qualifying hold on record does not qualify.

## Evidence

The hold tested is the account's most recent hardship hold as Ridgeline's records show it before the offer — its status, its ended date and its tier — and the hold tier's own figures decide the window and the eligibility.

## Hypothetical cases on the qualifying hold

| Most recent hold on the account (hypothetical) | Hold tier makes the account eligible after the hold | Qualifies for a Hardship Settlement |
|---|---|---|
| active | yes | yes |
| ended, ended date within the tier's post-hold window before the offer date | yes | yes |
| ended, ended date earlier than that window | yes | no |
| active or ended within the window | no | no |
| denied or withdrawn | — | no |
| none on record, consumer describes a hardship | — | no |

superseded_clauses: A Hardship Settlement is offered only when the account's most recent hardship hold is in status active, or has status ended with an ended_date no more than that hold tier's post_hold_hardship_window_days calendar days before the offer date, and in every case that hold tier's hardship_settlement_eligible_after_hold is true.
